newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA targets more Japanese, official says.
newsitem.headline: SIA targets more Japanese, official says.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) is working on a plan with the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board to attract more Japanese tourists to Singapore in 1997, SIA deputy managing director, commercial, Michael Tan, said on Thursday.
"It will be the last year before Hong Kong returns to China rule in 1997 and that is attracting a lot of Japanese tourists," Tan told reporters, speaking of a rival attraction to Singapore.
Tan, speaking at the launch of SIA's special audio headsets for its first class in-flight entertainment system, said Japan was a major market for Singapore as well as for SIA.
Japanese accounted for about 16 percent of tourist arrivals in Singapore and SIA operates more than 50 flights a week to Japan.
Tan said the plan included heavy advertising and promotion of Singapore and nearby countries and bringing Japanese tour agents into Singapore.

Yeoh Teng Kwong, SIA manager for inflight entertainment, said the airline's inflight entertainment system, which has been installed since the beginning of 1996, has generated some income from advertising.
Yeoh decline to give specific figures but said it was "a couple of million dollars".
The revenue is set to increase when the airline introduces gaming and electronic shopping on aircraft next year, he said.
